quote: Verknüpfungen von Elementenreihen, wofür das commu- tative Gesetz gilt und nicht das associative, und zweitens, für welche das associative gilt und nicht das commutative.
english: Compositions of series of elements for which the commutative law holds but not the associative law, and secondly, for which the associative law holds but not the commutative law.
topic: A list of research questions: reducing the number of parameters in an equation by solving equations of lower order, literature on equation theory in Mathematische Annalen, non-associative or non-commutative composition rules, and approximate counting of solutions of Diophantine inequalities by lattice points in a pyramid.

triage.modern_statement: This most likely asks about binary operations (magmas, algebras, number systems) that are commutative but not associative, and about ones that are associative but not commutative. It probably also asks what such operations do to arithmetic and to the foundations of geometry. In modern terms it is a program to study commutative non-associative structures (for example commutative quasigroups and loops, or Jordan algebras) and associative non-commutative structures (semigroups, groups, skew fields, matrix and quaternion algebras). The note gives no precise single statement to test.
triage.answered_by: No single paper answers this. The plain existence question was already settled before Hilbert: quaternions (Hamilton, 1843) and matrices are associative but not commutative, and simple commutative non-associative operations such as the mean x∘y=(x+y)/2 were easy to give. The deeper program was taken up later. Hilbert himself, in Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899), linked commutative multiplication to Pappus's theorem and built a non-commutative ordered field (an associative, non-commutative system), with Friedrich Schur working on the Pappus–commutativity link in 1898. Ruth Moufang (1933) used the non-associative octonions to build non-Desarguesian projective planes. Pascual Jordan (1932/33) introduced commutative non-associative Jordan algebras. These lines grew into the established fields of non-associative algebra and semigroup and ring theory.

evidence.claim: Hilbert studied how Pappus' theorem relates to commutative multiplication in a field in his 1899 Grundlagen der Geometrie, which ties geometry to systems that are associative but not commutative.
A historical case study traces the link between Pappus's theorem (collinearity) and commutativity, and notes that Friedrich Schur had also considered it in 1898.
In 1933 Ruth Moufang constructed a non-Desarguesian projective plane using the non-associative octonions.
Moufang planes are coordinatized by alternative division rings, which are rings that need not be associative.
Pascual Jordan introduced Jordan algebras, which are commutative non-associative algebras, in 1933 to axiomatize observables in quantum mechanics.
Non-associative algebras, including Jordan algebras and the octonions, are still studied in connection with physics.

triage.why: The note is a broad program ('study compositions with one law but not the other'), not a sharp conjecture. It is not one of the 23 Paris problems or the 24th problem. Read as an existence question it is elementary and was already answered by known examples. Read as a research program, Hilbert's own Grundlagen (1899) took up the associative-but-not-commutative side through Pappus's theorem and non-commutative fields. Later work by Moufang, Jordan and others created the theory of non-associative structures, which is still active. The sources do not show what Hilbert specifically meant by 'Elementenreihen', so linking the note to these later developments is an interpretation. Hence the low confidence.
